text:
Lina Chen: Quick check-in for Meridian account — weekly health snapshot + a couple of flags. Focus: p95/p99 latency by route/model and streaming vs non-streaming. TL;DR: streaming p99 for chat.generate jumped ~420ms on Wed evening; embedding routes stable. Suspect KV-cache cold starts and a burst of concurrent streams hitting shared pool.

Marco Ruiz: Looking at the traces now. Root cause looks like a combo of cache misses + a single node in the shared pool hitting OOM-triggered GC cycles at 2024-10-02T19:07:xxZ. Will paste the trace snippet. :eyes:

Marco Ruiz: ```
# trace filter
route=chat.generate model=redwood-1.3 pool=shared-streaming
span: kv_cache_miss -> backend_fetch (avg 12ms -> 320ms)
error: none, but tail latency escalates when concurrent_streams > 120
```

Priya Shah: Metric summary from Telemetry (p95 / p99 in ms) — timeframe Mon 00:00 -> Sun 23:59:
- chat.generate (redwood-1.3) streaming: p95=180ms, p99=620ms
- chat.generate (redwood-1.3) non-streaming: p95=95ms, p99=230ms
- chat.generate (redwood-lite-quant) streaming: p95=210ms, p99=710ms
- embed.create (redwood-emb-1) streaming: p95=85ms, p99=130ms
- summarize (redwood-1.3) non-streaming: p95=120ms, p99=260ms

Priya Shah: So streaming p99 is ~2.7x non-streaming for the main chat route. Embeddings are fine. Spending note: daily spend variance spiked +45% on Wed (unrelated high token counts), flagged for renewals team.

Ben Ortega: Suggested mitigations:
1) Temporarily offload high-concurrency streaming to a dedicated streaming pool for Meridian (reduces cross-tenant interference).
2) Enable more aggressive KV pre-warm for active onboarding sessions (TTL tuning).
3) Add per-account soft limits on concurrent streams to avoid noisy-neighbor P99 blowups.

Lina Chen: Action items:
- @Marco Ruiz to validate node GC/coredump and propose a mitigation timeline (ETA 24h).
- @Ben Ortega to spin up a dedicated streaming pool trial for Meridian and run A/B for 24h (ETA 48h).
- @Priya Shah to prepare a renewal risk note if spend variance persists (include cost projection).

Marco Ruiz: I ran a quick grep on node logs, saw a repeated pattern before spikes. Pasting the grep snippet:
```bash
sudo journalctl -u infer-runtime | grep -E "OOM|GC pause" | tail -n 40
# timestamps clustered 2024-10-02T19:05:xx -> 19:10:xx
```

Zoe (telemetry-bot): Automated alert: Meridian chat.generate streaming p99 exceeded threshold (600ms) at 2024-10-02T19:07:12Z. Recent baseline: 220ms.

Priya Shah: Customer touchpoint: Meridian CSM wants any perf regressions fixed before next onboarding wave (in 10 days). If we can't stabilize quickly, they'll consider shifting part of traffic to a competitor's hosted endpoint — renewal risk medium.

Lina Chen: Suggested communication draft to Meridian (short): "We're seeing a transient latency tail on streaming for chat.generate due to cache warmups and a noisy neighbor. We're spinning a dedicated pool for you and will share results within 48h. Apologies for the interruption — we'll keep you posted." Approve? :+1: / :-1:

Ben Ortega: :+1: from me. Also propose adding a quick perf dashboard tile they can view (read-only) so they can see progress in real time.

Marco Ruiz: I'll prioritize a hotfix to avoid the GC cycles and coordinate the pool spin-up with infra. Expecting 6h to test, 24h to validate in staging then flip in prod.

Priya Shah: I'll draft renewal note and attach the cost delta for dedicated pool vs shared burst. If we can show <5% SLA impact after fix, renewal risk drops to low.

Lina Chen: Cool. I'll send the customer draft after Marco's confirmation. Next check-in: 24h or sooner if Zoe flags p99 again. Thanks all. :rocket:
